S84.03.note: The Expected says 'system', but the picker's row for that is labelled Auto ('Match the terminal background'), and the choice is saved in the project's config, not for every folder.
steps: Open a terminal in the project folder, run agi and wait for the main screen.
Type /theme and press Enter. A Theme picker opens.
Move to Light with the arrow keys and press Enter.
Check that the screen recolours and a System line reads 'Theme set to Light, saved in ...'.
Quit agi, run agi again in the same folder and check the theme is still Light.
S84.03.where: Type /theme and press Enter in the agi terminal app, then pick Auto, Dark, Light or another row

S84.07.needs: a prompt that can be sent, so the busy spinner shows
S84.07.note: No code reads the OS reduce-motion setting; only the in-app setting, the --plain flag or AGI_PLAIN turn it on, and the effect found is on the busy spinner.
steps: Run agi in the project folder and wait for the main screen.
Type /config set reduced-motion true and press Enter. Read the reply: reduced-motion = true (saved).
Type /config show and press Enter. Look for the line 'Reduced motion: true'.
Send any short prompt so the app is busy. The spinner should stay as a still dot instead of turning.
Type /config set reduced-motion false to turn it back off and check the spinner animates again.
S84.07.where: Type /config set reduced-motion true in the agi terminal app (undo with false); check with /config show

S84.10.note: The Set arm in apps/cli/src/lib.rs (around line 4778-4785) prints the message and shows no save call, so it is unclear the default persists; the tester should verify with a new session.
steps: In a terminal, run agi models list to see catalog model IDs.
Run agi models set <one model ID from that list>.
Read the reply: Default model set to <model> (<provider>).
Start a new agi session in the same folder with agi and check the model shown matches the one you set (use /model to view it).
Compare with Expected: new conversations start with the chosen default model.
S84.10.where: In a terminal outside the app, run agi models set <model-id>; the in-app model picker is /model

S84.11.note: The default is saved per project (project config), not for every folder.
steps: Run agi in the project folder and wait for the main screen.
Type /effort and press Enter. An effort picker opens; choose a level and press Enter.
Or type /effort high and press Enter.
Read the reply: it says the effort was set and 'and saved as this project's default'.
Quit agi, start agi again in the same folder and check /effort shows the level you chose.
S84.11.where: Type /effort high (or /effort with no argument to open the effort picker) in the agi terminal app

S84.12.note: The code has permission modes (default, plan, auto, dontAsk), not chat versus agent; the bypassPermissions mode cannot be saved as a default, and an organisation policy can block a mode.
steps: In a terminal, run agi approvals mode to see the default mode new sessions start in.
Run agi approvals mode auto.
Read the reply: New sessions start in acceptEdits. (the saved name for auto)
Start a new agi session in the same folder and type /permissions to see the current mode.
Compare with Expected: a new conversation starts in the chosen mode.
S84.12.where: In a terminal outside the app, run agi approvals mode auto (view with agi approvals mode); in-app view is /permissions

S84.15.needs: access to the config.toml file to edit it
S84.15.note: Viewing is in the app, but customising is by editing config.toml; no in-app key editor was found, and disabling a shortcut was not confirmed in the code (the default for some actions is unbound).
steps: Run agi in the project folder and wait for the main screen.
Type /keybindings and press Enter. Read the Keybindings list with each key and its action.
To rebind, add a line under [ui.keybindings] in config.toml, for example open_palette = "ctrl+p", or run /config set ui.keybindings.open_palette ctrl+p.
Quit agi, start it again and type /keybindings.
Compare the shown key for that action with the new value.
S84.15.where: Type /keybindings (or /keys) in the agi terminal app to view; customise by editing the [ui.keybindings] table in config.toml
